_README: EQLS Auras is Shara's project. Shara has creative and production control over it and her copy reaches this file through the owner. NOTHING IN HERE MAY BE WRITTEN BY A BUILD SESSION. The fields below were moved verbatim out of _build/build1.py on 1 Sep 2026 so that the home-page band and /auras.html read one source instead of two; not a word of them was authored here. Fill download.url and media.gallery and the page grows to fit. Leave a field null and the page omits it rather than inventing it.
name: EQLS Auras
lede: It reads your combat log and draws your buffs over the game as icons that count down, so you can see what is about to drop off without opening a window.
body: It reads files the client already has: the log it writes as you play, your spellbook, and the game’s own spell icons. It does not read or alter the game’s memory, inject code into it, or send it input. It fetches its typeface from Google each time it launches, which discloses your IP address to Google; beyond that it sends nothing — no telemetry, no analytics, no update check. That fetch is the main window only: the overlay drawn over the game requests nothing at all.
The idea is WeakAuras’. The code is not: a from-scratch implementation for EverQuest Legends, sharing no code and no trigger format with it, and neither affiliated with nor endorsed by its authors.

download._note: Fill url with the real download address and the page renders a download control. While it is null the page says nothing about how to get it, because there is no true thing to say. NEVER put a guessed URL here.

_links_note: Optional. Each entry {"href": ..., "label": ..., "note": ...}. Somewhere it runs, a guide, a place to report a problem. Empty renders nothing.

media._gallery_note: Keys into assets/media.json. Drop Shara's stills or GIFs into _media/, run python3 _build/media.py, then list their keys here — e.g. ["auras-timers", "auras-setup"]. Each renders in a fixed 16:9 slot, so adding one moves no layout. An animated GIF is treated as an image and is not motion-gated; prefer a video for anything long.
